companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At age 3, you made time to play together.
At age 10, you made time to play together.
At age 17, you made time to walk the familiar trails together.
We began traveling together after growing up as friends.

You accept work guarding the threshold for willing observers. The door is covered between vigils, and the trapped sky remains still. The keeper allows the watch but continues waiting for its last observation.
You accept work tending the shutter for the nearby households. The visitor waits outside, quiet during the agreed watch. Its old welcome remains beneath the sill, unread and unrenewed.
You accept paid watch from the nearby households. You cover the opening between agreed vigils and learn which movement of the bell stills the figure, leaving it below rather than releasing it.
You tend the niche for its paying keepers and record when the mask speaks. Its unfinished watch becomes a guarded curiosity; the old release remains partly covered beneath the iron.

You tend the branch for paying listeners who choose to attend. The shadows speak only when addressed, then fold back into their leaves. Their release remains unfinished, but the vigils are quiet rather than forced.
You threaten to leave the threshold open unless nearby households pay. The keeper covers its face as the black star presses forward. The witness remembers who turned an unfinished rite into a ransom.

You damage the welcome mark and threaten to erase the last of it. The visitor remains caught in the wall while frightened households pay your demands. The witness hears its wings grow louder when you leave.
You sound the lower bell until its reflections rise into the upper opening. Frightened households pay for your promise to keep them down. The witness remembers that the voices were asking to leave.
You use the shadows beyond the slit to demand payment and obedience. The mask repeats your warning in its old commander’s voice. The witness remembers the confession you prevented it from finishing.
You bruise the silver roots until the shadows speak their most painful memories. Frightened listeners pay to stop the hearing. The witness remembers the names that asked to remain silent.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Aeseth Petalbough was born in Amberwell Crossing. The morning brought low fog.

journal.title: Your origin
journal.text: Borderborn. Your first blanket belongs to a household driven from its home. Your guardians find shelter across an unfamiliar border. A shelter guardian cares for you while a lasting home is sought. Your cradle belonged to Displaced households.

journal.title: A second name in the register
journal.text: Karyen Sandcourt gives your name firmly. The keeper crosses out the other one, but presses too lightly to hide it completely.

journal.title: A temporary roof
journal.text: Karyen Sandcourt secured local shelter without a fee. Secure ownership can grow later through an actual home or building project.

journal.title: The Returning Shape
journal.text: A familiar shape leans close, disappears and returns. You cannot count the returns, but your body knows the difference between waiting and being held.

journal.title: A Low Note
journal.text: A low hum is easier to follow than speech. For a little while, each breath seems to carry the same note through the dark.

journal.title: Before Words
journal.text: A voice repeats the same soft sounds. You do not know the story inside them; you know the pause before the voice begins again.

journal.title: The song at the cradle
journal.text: The tune remains. Years later, you know exactly where the new words do not quite fit.

journal.title: Steps Beyond Sight
journal.text: Footsteps pass somewhere beyond your view: near, then far, then gone. You turn toward the sound before there is a word for where it went.

journal.title: The Small Hours
journal.text: You wake while the world is quiet, then drift away before it has finished waking. The hours belong to bodily needs rather than bells or promises.

journal.title: Light on the Wall
journal.text: A patch of light moves beyond your reach. Your eyes follow it until it breaks into shadow. No kingdom could be larger than that wall today.

journal.title: Boots at the threshold
journal.text: You cry at the closing door. The neighbor shows you how to tap a spoon against a cup until you forget the puddle.

journal.title: No Name for Morning
journal.text: The dark thins. Sounds begin again, one after another. You have no name for morning; it arrives all the same, asking only that you wake.

journal.title: The Edge of Cloth
journal.text: Your fingers close around a fold of cloth. The rough weave, the warmth beneath it and the effort of holding on fill the whole moment.

journal.title: The Shape of a Hand
journal.text: A hand enters your small world. You study its shifting outline, then your own fingers, with the grave attention of someone meeting a mystery for the first time.

journal.title: The blackberry rule
journal.text: Your sleeve tears on the fence. The berries stain your mouth purple, and Savaelun Lindenmemory finally makes room in the game.

journal.title: A nature taking shape
journal.text: Your patient nature becomes part of your choices and abilities.

journal.title: Play with Nerrina Musselcross
journal.text: Play with Nerrina Musselcross: your survival skill grew. Your identity remains yours to choose.

journal.title: A small pleasure
journal.text: Age 3, day 1097: You found 2 extra joy in sharing a familiar trail with Nerrina Musselcross. Enjoyment follows what you actually do, and can return after 30 days.

journal.title: A conversation with Karyen Sandcourt
journal.text: A kingdom made of chalk. You said: “You can choose what happens next.” Karyen Sandcourt replied: “Then our castle has a door that everyone can use.”

journal.title: The Giant at Your Feet
journal.text: Your shadow runs farther than you do. In a bent angle of light, it briefly wears the stature of someone who knows every road out of Amberwell Crossing.

journal.title: A Familiar Name in the Day
journal.text: Heskum of Tongs remains a living person in your world, beyond the last conversation you remember. A friendship contains separate days as well as the ones its people share.

journal.title: The Ordinary Monster
journal.text: A knot in wood has the face of a little horned thing from a frightening story. From another angle it looks worried. You wonder whether monsters ever frighten themselves.

journal.title: The moth in the jar
journal.text: You fall asleep counting the taps against the glass. Karyen Sandcourt finds the jar beneath your pillow at dawn.

journal.title: The Cinderbound omen · age 4
journal.text: At four, a cold fireplace shows unfamiliar hands tending its coals. Only the person beside you sees you reach toward them.

journal.title: A conversation with Heskum of Tongs
journal.text: Something the world remembers. You said: “Whatever it means, I still want a life of my own.” Heskum of Tongs replied: “You are allowed that. A sign does not own the person who notices it.”

journal.title: A Question Too Large
journal.text: You wonder where the dark goes when morning comes. Nothing at Amberwell Crossing gives an answer, but the unanswered question feels less frightening in daylight.

journal.title: The game behind the locked gate
journal.text: Caevera Petalbough has made a small fort from packing crates. Heskum of Tongs tells the younger children it is full, although there is a whole bench inside. Your sibling taps twice on the gate and waits. You know the game they are playing; you also know who owns the crates.

journal.title: The Secret of Names
journal.text: Places seem more solid after you learn their names. Still, a dark corner remains a dark corner no matter how confidently you call it by an ordinary word.

journal.title: The game behind the locked gate
journal.text: Caevera Petalbough has made a small fort from packing crates. Alauven Drygarden tells the younger children it is full, although there is a whole bench inside. Your sibling taps twice on the gate and waits. You know the game they are playing; you also know who owns the crates.

journal.title: Where the Stone Must Move
journal.text: The gate’s great outline depends on small moving parts. A hinge carries what a carved crest can only announce.

journal.title: Something kept from your first night
journal.text: Karyen Sandcourt closes the record. That evening, the light beneath the hearth looks ordinary again.

journal.title: A conversation with Caevera Petalbough
journal.text: Something the world remembers. You said: “I need to understand more before I explain the details.” Caevera Petalbough replied: “Then take care, and remember that keeping a secret is not the same as being alone.”

journal.title: A Very Important Stone
journal.text: A stone becomes a tower, a dragon’s tooth and then only a stone again. The world has not grown less strange because the names keep changing.

journal.title: The place beside the window
journal.text: Caevera Petalbough pulls a bench toward the window. Heskum of Tongs puts a slate in the gap before anyone can sit down. Yesterday the two of them shared their lunch; today neither looks at the other. The rest of the table waits to see where you sit.

journal.title: A Mark of Height
journal.text: A low shelf no longer seems quite so high. Growing is rarely something you notice as it happens; today, the world gives you a small piece of evidence.

journal.title: The Late Season
journal.text: The year enters its last season. Whatever its weather brings to Amberwell Crossing, the calendar is drawing a boundary through lives that will continue across it.

journal.title: The jump across the ditch
journal.text: You land with one foot on the far bank and one in the water. Savaelun Lindenmemory gives you the copper anyway.

journal.title: A door into named lessons

choices.label: Settle the verified amount privately
choices.outcome: You settle the small verified sum through a paid accounting job. The demand for obedience stays outside the agreement.

choices.label: Forge a claim that gives you the only key
choices.outcome: You alter the claim and obtain the key. A witness retains a copy of the earlier agreement.

choices.label: Resolve the claim in front of willing witnesses
choices.outcome: The remaining terms are read aloud and limited to what was actually agreed. The household keeps a copy beside its own names.

choices.label: Buy a clearly credited copy
choices.outcome: You negotiate a fee and retain the fieldworker’s credit. The patron pays you to prepare the final account.

choices.label: Undermine their patron with a false report
choices.outcome: You send a false report about the rival’s work. The patron suspends their support; your rival knows which claim was invented.

choices.label: Keep the disagreement beside a joint correction
choices.outcome: The archive keeps both earlier accounts and the joint correction. Rivalry becomes a continuing exchange of evidence.

choices.label: Negotiate a limited replacement
choices.outcome: You agree a replacement within a stated limit. The patron pays for the work, but the wider fault remains unexamined.

choices.label: Pressure the witness to withdraw
choices.outcome: You threaten the witness with the patron’s displeasure. They withdraw their public complaint and retain a private copy.

choices.label: Publish the fault and teach the correction
choices.outcome: The correction becomes part of the local workshop record, with the households’ names included by agreement.

choices.label: Take the estate’s paid work
choices.outcome: You finish the estate’s repairs for a written fee. The common beds depend on the households who can still spare time.

choices.label: Withhold supplies to demand obedience
choices.outcome: You hold supplies until households accept your terms. They eat, but the winter list now records who depended on your permission.

choices.label: Give the commons a charter of its own
choices.outcome: The seed account belongs to the participating households. New members can see how shares and disagreements are recorded.

choices.label: Take paid watch over the moonlit threshold
choices.outcome: You accept work guarding the threshold for willing observers. The door is covered between vigils, and the trapped sky remains still. The keeper allows the watch but continues waiting for its last observation.

choices.label: Use the dark star to force a richer protection bargain
choices.outcome: You threaten to leave the threshold open unless nearby households pay. The keeper covers its face as the black star presses forward. The witness remembers who turned an unfinished rite into a ransom.

choices.label: Take paid watch over the unopened window
choices.outcome: You accept work tending the shutter for the nearby households. The visitor waits outside, quiet during the agreed watch. Its old welcome remains beneath the sill, unread and unrenewed.

choices.label: Hold the visitor between wall and shadow for ransom
choices.outcome: You damage the welcome mark and threaten to erase the last of it. The visitor remains caught in the wall while frightened households pay your demands. The witness hears its wings grow louder when you leave.

choices.label: Keep a paid night watch over the opening
choices.outcome: You accept paid watch from the nearby households. You cover the opening between agreed vigils and learn which movement of the bell stills the figure, leaving it below rather than releasing it.

choices.label: Make the lower voices an instrument of fear
choices.outcome: You sound the lower bell until its reflections rise into the upper opening. Frightened households pay for your promise to keep them down. The witness remembers that the voices were asking to leave.

choices.label: Take a paid commission to examine the speaking niche
choices.outcome: You tend the niche for its paying keepers and record when the mask speaks. Its unfinished watch becomes a guarded curiosity; the old release remains partly covered beneath the iron.

choices.label: Threaten listeners with the kneeling road
choices.outcome: You use the shadows beyond the slit to demand payment and obedience. The mask repeats your warning in its old commander’s voice. The witness remembers the confession you prevented it from finishing.

choices.label: Keep paid, willing vigils beside the silver leaves
choices.outcome: You tend the branch for paying listeners who choose to attend. The shadows speak only when addressed, then fold back into their leaves. Their release remains unfinished, but the vigils are quiet rather than forced.

choices.label: Force the leaves to reveal what their listeners fear
choices.outcome: You bruise the silver roots until the shadows speak their most painful memories. Frightened listeners pay to stop the hearing. The witness remembers the names that asked to remain silent.
